title: I Almost Quit YouTube... But Here’s Why I Didn’t! | Slow English for Beginner/Intermediate Learners
channel: Speak English with Bo's Slow English

lines.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to a new episode
of Bose's Slow English. In today's
episode, I want to talk about my journey
and experience as a
YouTuber. I just hit 3,000 subscribers.
Uh, I started my channel in May of
2024. So, it's we're approaching one
year and I'm proud of the progress that
I've made. Before I go on, please hit
the like button to show your support and
hit subscribe to receive almost daily
English lessons. A few years ago, I
started learning French. And my favorite
way of learning French is by watching
slowspeaking French vlogs on YouTube. I
think that was the most efficient way
for me to understand how a native
speaker speaks. So, I was bored one day
and I searched on YouTube slow English
vlogs and I realized there's not many
out there unless it's just not showing
up on my feed. So that night I said, I'm
going to make a YouTube
channel. That's just how my brain works.
When I have an idea, I usually jump on
the idea as soon as possible. Um,
otherwise I can't sleep because I'll
just constantly think about the idea and
the thought of the idea instead of just
doing it. I didn't have this fancy vlog
camera that I'm using now. I just had my
iPhone and I learned the process of
vlogging, which means that you look into
the camera and you just talk. Making
these videos takes
maybe 20 to 30 minutes. I'll watch TV
for 30 minutes and I could be filming a
YouTube video. So, I decided to cut out
some of the daily habits that I have so
that I could make room to film. I had a
lot of doubt at first because my
subscriber count and my views were very
low. But with
consistency, I did start to see the
numbers go up. If I'm going to be very
honest, last week I told my husband, I
don't know if I want to continue
YouTube because I have so much going on
outside of YouTube in my life. I want to
make sure that if I'm committed to
something that I give it my all. I
almost quit
YouTube, but then I said I I've already
invested almost a year into this. I
can't quit. So, this week I posted two
long videos, which are these type of
videos, not the shorts. and I've never
had so many views and likes and
comments. So, that was very encouraging.
So, the life of a part-time YouTube
vlogger can be demanding.
In other words, it requires a lot of
work, but in my opinion, it's rewarding,
especially when I see comments of
nonnative English speakers saying that
my videos were helpful for them in their
English learning journey. So, here is
the general process of how making a
video and uploading a video works.
First, you should research within your
niche, which is the audience or category
that you are speaking to, and see what
kind of videos and topics are attracting
an audience. And then you turn on a
camera and you just do it.
That is the best way to learn is just to
experience. After you feel like you have
good enough, not perfect but good enough
content that would be helpful for your
audience. You will upload the video to
your laptop or computer. I use a
software called Cap Cut. I knew nothing
about Cap Cut and now I know enough to
create basic vlog videos with basic
editing. If you are considering using
Cap Cut and you have any basic
questions, feel free to leave a comment
and I would be happy to answer you with
the best of my ability. I'm no expert,
but I want to be helpful. So there was
quite a learning curve with learning how
to edit. But once you get that down,
then the flow and efficiency of the
whole editing process can be done. Not
quickly, but maybe for like a 15-minute
video, it takes me 45 minutes to an hour
to edit. And I actually find a lot of
joy in the editing process because it's
an art. So after you finish editing your
video, then you download it and you
upload it into YouTube. You have to
think about what caption to write, what
description to write. And this is based
on key words that your audience would be
attracted to, but also based on what has
worked in the past with other
YouTubers that are in your niche. Again,
niche is like the category that you're
working in. And that's that's the
summary of how that works. And once you
upload it, you do it again. So it needs
to be consistent. Sometimes I will spend
an hour to two
researching what my next topic should be
and I will just sit in front of the
camera and bang out a bunch of shorts.
Bang out is an idiom which means I just
get it done and throughout the week I
will edit those YouTube shorts on Cap
Cut. I had a YouTube mentor at one point
and his suggestion was to post one to
two YouTube shorts per day in order for
your channel to grow. And I was doing
that for
um maybe 6 to 7 months. But as of last
week, the week that I decided that I
wanted to quit
YouTube,
I posted two long videos and I received
more traction with the videos. Traction
means more likes, comments, more
subscribers. I'm going to switch my
method of growing my channel and I'm
going to be posting more long videos
instead of short videos. I also think
that the viewers of the long videos will
sit and actively watch your videos more
than the people who will watch your
shorts videos. they probably won't watch
it more than one to two
times. And in order to become monetized
on YouTube, which I'm nowhere near, the
amount of hours watched has to be 4,000
watch hours for the long videos and 10
million watch hours for the short
videos. But there is a time restriction
on this. 4,000 hours for long videos has
to be within
365 days or 1 year. And the time to meet
your 10 million shorts views has to be
within 90 days. And personally for me, I
seem to be growing faster or getting
more views on the long videos. Although
my eventual goal is to get monetized on
YouTube, I know that it's going to take
an extremely long time. And I've learned
to build some patience and enjoy the
process. My driving force in life which
is my purpose in life is to teach
people, connect people and to be
helpful. And I get a lot of joy from
teaching and being helpful for my
non-English subscribers. So, let me know
in the comments. Have you ever
considered being a YouTuber and was
curious about the process of how all
this works? I'd love to know. Let me
know in the comments. And thank you for
watching my video. I hope you have a
wonderful day. And feel free to comment
if you have any feedback or would like
to suggest the topic of the next video.
Bye. Thank you.
